research_question_and_methods.justification: objective_and_hypothesis: Meets the score 3 description: the paper states explicit, testable questions about DENV-2-backbone skewing and immune imprinting, and applies longitudinal neutralization and cellular assays directly to these questions. The rationale is clearly linked to tetravalent protection and potential antibody-dependent enhancement risk. | public_health_relevance: Meets the score 3 description: dengue is identified as a major global health threat, and the study explicitly relates its vaccine question to the documented record dengue surge in the Americas during 2024. The work addresses a current outbreak-relevant vaccination and protection gap. | study_design_rigor: Meets the score 3 description: this is a clearly described longitudinal cohort of 99 retained participants, sampled at four defined timepoints after two Qdenga doses, with baseline-serostatus stratification, blinded laboratory testing, detailed FRNT/ELISA/flow-cytometry methods, vaccine and circulating-virus validation, and stated source-data availability.

objective_and_hypothesis.justification: Meets the score 3 description: the paper states explicit, testable questions about DENV-2-backbone skewing and immune imprinting, and applies longitudinal neutralization and cellular assays directly to these questions. The rationale is clearly linked to tetravalent protection and potential antibody-dependent enhancement risk.
objective_and_hypothesis.quote: We investigated whether the vaccine design skews responses to the DENV-2 backbone and assessed the extent to which immune imprinting (prior DENV exposure) shapes the magnitude and breadth of the vaccine responses.

public_health_relevance.justification: Meets the score 3 description: dengue is identified as a major global health threat, and the study explicitly relates its vaccine question to the documented record dengue surge in the Americas during 2024. The work addresses a current outbreak-relevant vaccination and protection gap.
public_health_relevance.quote: the Americas reporting a record 12.6 million cases in 2024, nearly triple the previous year's number

study_design_rigor.justification: Meets the score 3 description: this is a clearly described longitudinal cohort of 99 retained participants, sampled at four defined timepoints after two Qdenga doses, with baseline-serostatus stratification, blinded laboratory testing, detailed FRNT/ELISA/flow-cytometry methods, vaccine and circulating-virus validation, and stated source-data availability.
study_design_rigor.quote: All ELISA, FRNT, and flow cytometry analyses were performed in a blinded manner by independent laboratory teams.

results_and_conclusion.justification: Matches the score 2 description: Figures 1–4 and the FRNT testing of both vaccine and circulating strains support the main serotype-skewing findings, including Figure 4's reported 63%, 76%, 61%, and 12% responder rates for DENV-1–4, and limitations are discussed. However, reporting is internally inconsistent: page 4 reports an acute coronary syndrome after dose two, whereas Methods states no serious adverse events, and Figure 1 specifies a 3-SD T-cell positivity threshold while Methods specifies 2 SD.
results_and_conclusion.quote: No serious adverse events were reported following Qdenga vaccination (Table S2).

references.justification: The references combine authoritative WHO surveillance with peer-reviewed foundational dengue/ADE studies, TAK-003 phase 2/3 efficacy and safety studies, recent dengue epidemiology, and relevant immune-imprinting and aging-immunology literature. No clearly unrelated reference was identified; the organizational WHO fact sheet is appropriate for disease-burden context.
references.quote: Katzelnick, L. C. et al. Antibody-dependent enhancement of severe dengue disease in humans.
